title: Progressive Era
examples: What were the main goals of the Progressive movement?
How did muckraking journalism influence government policy?
Can you compare the reforms before and after this era?

explain.say: The Progressive Era saw many efforts to reform society. People wanted to improve daily life for everyone.
One major reform area was in city sanitation and housing. Cities needed cleaner air and safer homes.
Another key reform targeted industrial labor laws. Workers needed safer places to do their jobs.
Muckrakers were journalists who exposed social problems. They brought hidden issues into public view.
For example, Upton Sinclair wrote about the meatpacking industry. His book showed unsanitary conditions to the public.
In real life, think about modern food safety laws. They are a direct result of these early efforts.

faq.q: What was the main difference between a reformer and a muckraker?
faq.a: A reformer was often the person pushing for the change, while a muckraker was the journalist who exposed the problem first. You might also ask, 'Who pushed for the laws?' or 'What was the role of the press here?'
asks: Was it the reporters or the politicians?

faq.q: Did the Progressive Era end because the reforms were successful?
faq.a: The movement didn't end cleanly; it evolved and was challenged by other social movements. You could also ask, 'What came after the big reforms?' or 'Was the progress permanent?'
asks: What was the next big social movement?

faq.q: Were the reforms only for poor people in cities?
faq.a: No, the reforms addressed issues across society, including business practices and education standards. You might ask, 'Did everyone benefit equally?' or 'Were there rich people affected?'
asks: Was it just about city life?
Did the reforms cover all classes?

faq.a: It was the act of investigating and writing about corruption or social ills. It meant digging up the 'gunk' or dirt on powerful people. You could also ask, 'What did muckrakers write about?' or 'What does 'muckraking' mean?'
asks: What kind of journalism was it?
Did they just write bad stories?

faq.q: Were the reforms always passed by Congress?
faq.a: Sometimes state governments passed laws, and sometimes federal action was needed. The pressure from the public helped push both levels of government. You might ask, 'Who passed the laws?' or 'Was it state or national action?'
asks: Did the government pass the laws?
Was it a local or national issue?

facts: Progressive Era reformers sought to use government power to solve social problems.
Muckrakers used investigative journalism to reveal corruption and unsafe practices.
Key reforms included improvements in public health, safety, and labor conditions.
The movement was a broad effort involving activists, journalists, and politicians.
